routes.label: Locate the median by cumulative counts

officialSolution.label: 2021 AMC 12A

question:
In the following list of numbers, the integer \(n\) appears \(n\) times in the list for \(1 \le n \le 200.\) \(1,\) \(2,\) \(2,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(4,\) \(4,\) \(4,\) \(\ldots,\) \(200,\) \(200,\) \(\ldots,\) \(200\)

What is the median of the numbers in this list?
solution:
Because each integer \(n\) contributes \(n\) entries, cumulative sums locate the middle entries of the list.

The total number of entries is
\[
1+2+\cdots+200=\frac{200\cdot201}{2}=20{,}100.
\]
This is even, so the median is the average of the entries in positions \(10{,}050\) and \(10{,}051\).

The number of entries with value at most \(n\) is
\[
1+2+\cdots+n=\frac{n(n+1)}2.
\]
Near the middle positions, we have
\[
\frac{141\cdot142}{2}=10{,}011,
\qquad
\frac{142\cdot143}{2}=10{,}153.
\]
Thus the entries equal to \(142\) occupy positions \(10{,}012\) through \(10{,}153\). Both middle positions lie in this range, so the median is
\[
\frac{142+142}{2}=\boxed{142},
\]
which is choice \(\text{C}\).
